subject: Localized storage guarantees and temporary replication / SLA exception language
messages:
From: 'Acme Analytics' <security@acme-analytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@acme-analytics.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on localized storage during maintenance windows

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. A couple of items we need to lock down before we escalate procurement:

- Can Redwood confirm that primary customer content for Acme Analytics (production request/response payloads and associated logs used for billing/debugging) will remain stored and processed within our selected EU region (Frankfurt) except for limited, documented operational exceptions?
- We understand there are maintenance/upgrade procedures that may require transient replication to another region for failover or live migration. We need clarification on: expected max duration for such transient replication, whether it will be encrypted in-transit AND at-rest in the destination region, and the exact subprocessors that may access data during that window.
- Finally, procurement has asked for a short contractual clause we can attach to the DPA that enumerates the exception conditions (planned maintenance, DR failover, degraded hardware) and an SLA on notification and retention of replication artifacts.

Attachments: I attached our baseline DPA annex (DPA-Annex-A-redwood-draft-v3.pdf) with inline comments on residency language.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a signed commitment for: (1) localized storage between requests, (2) a maximum 24-hour ephemeral replication window for scheduled maintenance, and (3) KMS separation (customer-managed keys for EU keys)?

Appreciate a clear list of subprocessors that would be involved in any cross-region operation.

—Daniel Rivera
Security Lead, Acme Analytics
security@acme-analytics.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on localized storage during maintenance windows

Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Quick reply while we pull legal/infra details:

Summary answers (high level):
- Localized storage: yes — normal serving and persisted artifacts are kept in the customer-chosen region (we already provide region-scoped object stores and local KV caches).
- Transient replication: supported for planned maintenance and DR failover; we treat these as operational exceptions and minimize scope. We recommend a maximum "ephemeral replication" window of 24 hours for scheduled maintenance; automated failover windows for unplanned DR may be slightly longer while we validate consistency. All replication traffic is TLS 1.3 and destinations are encrypted at-rest where supported.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) in EU regions; there are a few nuances for on-prem HSMs which we can detail.

Next steps: Vivek will provide the exact subprocessors involved and a short, contractual clause proposal. Mina will propose DPA wording for the annex that enumerates exceptions, notification timing, and retention of replication artifacts. I’ll assemble a short playbook (egress-playbook-summary.docx) that we can attach.

I expect a draft clause back by end of day Monday. If procurement needs the clause sooner for routing to legal, flag and I’ll prioritize.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 07:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on localized storage during maintenance windows

Karthik / Laura — adding infra detail for Acme:

- Subprocessors: the only third parties that touch ephemeral replicated blobs during a transient replication window are (1) our cloud provider's managed storage service in the target region (listed in the attached roster), and (2) our monitoring/ops vendor who has read-only access to replication logs for debugging (these accesses are audited). We do not run analytics or ML training on replicated customer data.
- Duration: for planned maintenance we propose a contractual cap of 24 hours; for emergency failovers we will document an "extended window" process requiring incident report and customer notification within 4 hours of detection, and a post-incident attestation within 72 hours.
- Encryption & key separation: replication is encrypted in-transit (TLS 1.3) and at-rest by default. For EU keys you can supply CMKs (customer-managed keys); if a CMK is used we will not have decryption key access.
- Artifacts retention: replication snapshots created solely for migration are retained only until consistency checks complete; we will include a retention max (7 days) in the DPA annex for auditability.

Attaching: subprocessor-roster-2026-10.csv and a short egres s playbook summary (egress-playbook-summary.docx).

Vivek
Director, Infrastructure Services

Daniel / Acme contracts team — thanks for the patience. Attached is proposed language for Annex A (localized storage + exception windows) that Mina drafted with infra input:

Proposed (excerpt):
"Redwood will keep Customer Content within the geographical region designated by the Customer for normal processing and storage. Except as expressly enumerated below, Redwood will not transfer Customer Content outside the designated region. Operational exceptions include: (a) planned maintenance requiring ephemeral replication to a nearest compatible region for data migration or live upgrade; (b) emergency disaster recovery failover where infrastructure health requires routing to alternate region to maintain availability. Except as required by law, such exceptions will only occur as described below.

For planned maintenance, Redwood will: (i) limit ephemeral replication to a maximum of 24 hours per maintenance event, (ii) encrypt replication in-transit and at-rest, (iii) notify the Customer at least 48 hours in advance and provide the target region and subprocessors involved.

For emergency failovers, Redwood will: (i) notify Customer within 4 hours of failover initiation, (ii) provide a post-incident attestation detailing the scope and duration of cross-region processing within 72 hours, and (iii) delete any migration artifacts within seven (7) days except as required for audit.

When Customer elects to use Customer-Managed Keys (CMKs) in the designated region, Redwood will not possess the key material and will be unable to decrypt data without Customer consent.

—End excerpt—

Action items for Acme: please confirm whether the proposed caps (24-hour planned window, 7-day artifact retention) are acceptable and whether the 48-hour advance notice for planned maintenance meets your procurement requirements. If yes, we will enter this as an addendum to the DPA and route for signature (DocuSign link below).
